title: Tibetan Empire
summary: Tibet's recorded history begins with the emperor Songtsen Gampo (c. 617-649), who united the peoples of the Tibetan plateau and sent armies deep into neighbouring lands; a Tibetan writing system was created in his reign. His marriage to the Chinese princess of Wencheng brought a famed Buddha image to his capital, Lhasa, where the Jokhang temple was founded in the seventh century. Later emperors sponsored Buddhism and vast translation projects. After the emperor Langdarma was killed in 842, the empire soon collapsed.

uncertainty.note: Traditional accession dates for Songtsen Gampo range from 617/618 to 629; the empire collapsed into civil war and division after the death of Langdarma in 842 (with remnant struggles extending to c. 850).
